title: Beatrix and the Drop
premise: Quentin Okafor, a private security contractor who guards clients nobody trusts, is approached by a stranger named Beatrix who claims he once saved her life — a favor he has no memory of. She repays it with information: the encrypted 'drop' hidden in his own security firm's servers contains proof that the governments hiring his company have been laundering assassinations through his contracts. As Quentin and Beatrix race to extract and broadcast the drop, they are hunted by an assassin codenamed Vesper, whose kill list includes everyone who has ever touched the file. In the border town of Kesselheim, with the checkpoint shifts changing in hours, Quentin must choose between the rules that kept him alive for seven years and the found family he never meant to build — and the truth gets out only because Beatrix sacrifices her anonymity, trading her freedom to buy Quentin's escape and the story's release.
about_author: Yara Lockridge is a former logistics coordinator for humanitarian convoys who writes thrillers about people caught between institutions and their consciences. She lives near a land border she crosses often, and says every checkpoint is a story waiting to happen.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A woman named Beatrix appears at Quentin's office claiming he saved her life in Lagos seven years ago — an event he cannot recall. She leaves a burner phone and a warning: 'interest is owed.' The beat is unease; Quentin's ordered world develops its first hairline crack.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Quentin runs background checks on Beatrix and finds nothing — no records before six years ago. His firm's new client contract arrives with clauses he's never seen, quietly expanding liability onto contractors. Emotional beat: professional paranoia sharpening into instinct.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. We learn Beatrix's side: she did meet Quentin once, and what he actually did that night. She reveals the first fragment — his firm's servers hold something called 'the Drop.' Beat: reluctant trust between two people who both survive by trusting no one.

chapters.title: Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A routine protection detail goes wrong when Quentin realizes the 'threat' his client fears is a witness the client himself arranged to silence. He aborts the job, breaking protocol for the first time. Beat: the moment loyalty to rules becomes complicity.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: POV assassin (unnamed). Introduce the assassin reviewing a kill list tied to the Drop — Quentin's name is on it, added that morning. Cold, procedural chapters establish the antagonist's methodical patience. Beat: dread through competence.

chapters.title: The Server Room
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix and Quentin break into his own firm after hours and find the Drop: an encrypted archive logging off-book operations laundered through legitimate contracts. They copy nothing yet — the archive is tripwired. Beat: vertigo at discovering your employer is the crime scene.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Quentin maps which agencies are implicated and realizes there is no authority left to report to — all three potential recipients are compromised. Beatrix proposes going public instead. Beat: the collapse of institutional faith, the birth of a plan.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Hiding in a safehouse, the two calculate odds and resources; Beatrix reveals her network of fellow 'returned favors' — strangers bound by debts, a loose found family. Beat: warmth kindling inside tradecraft.

chapters.title: First Blood
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. One of Beatrix's contacts is killed with surgical precision — Vesper's calling card. Quentin understands the hunt has begun and that every person who helps them becomes a target. Beat: guilt as fuel.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Town
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. They travel to Kesselheim, a border town where the Drop can be uploaded via a journalist's satellite uplink during the eight-hour window when checkpoint shifts change and surveillance thins. Beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Meeting with embittered journalist Ilse Brandt, who agrees to publish but demands verification — meaning someone must decrypt the full archive, not fragments. Beat: alliance formed out of mutual disillusionment.

chapters.title: What Beatrix Buried
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Flashback chapter: Beatrix's true history — she was an analyst who built part of the laundering system before defecting; her 'favor' from Quentin was real but not what she claimed. Beat: confession, and the risk that honesty destroys the alliance.

chapters.title: Tripwire
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The firm detects the server intrusion; Quentin's former colleagues — men he trained — are deployed to find him. Betrayal hits personally. Beat: the found family of the firm revealed as a cage.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: POV assassin. Vesper arrives in Kesselheim ahead of them, mapping the checkpoint rotations and identifying the upload window. The reader now knows something the protagonists don't. Beat: dramatic irony tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: Decryption Night
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Working from a farmhouse, Beatrix decrypts the archive while Quentin watches the roads. Inside: names, dates, payments — including proof that Vesper's kills were contracted through the very system. Beat: horror and resolve fused.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Mill
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Vesper strikes the farmhouse. Quentin and Beatrix barely escape; Ilse's backup drive is destroyed; Beatrix is wounded. Beat: the cost made physical, the plan down to one fragile copy.

chapters.title: Debts Called In
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix calls in every favor in her network — the returned-favors family mobilizes, creating decoys across three countries. Beat: the theme made action; belonging as strategy.

chapters.title: The Long Window
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The night of the shift change begins. Decoys draw Vesper's attention while Quentin carries the decrypted archive toward Ilse's uplink through the checkpoint's blind hours. Beat: sustained suspense, ticking clock.

chapters.title: Face to Face
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Vesper corners Beatrix at the fallback point. Instead of running, Beatrix offers her the truth: Vesper's own name is in the archive as disposable. The assassin hesitates — and lets her go, or believes she does. Beat: moral rupture in the antagonist.

chapters.title: Upload
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. At the uplink, Quentin is caught between Vesper arriving and the transfer completing. He chooses to stay with the machine until the last packet clears, taking a bullet rather than aborting. Beat: climax — sacrifice over survival, truth past everything.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV multiple brief. The Drop publishes worldwide; resignations cascade; Vesper vanishes, list unfinished. Beatrix turns herself in to protect Quentin, using her testimony as shield. Beat: bittersweet victory — truth wins, freedom doesn't.

chapters.title: Beatrix and the Drop
chapters.summary: POV Quentin, months later. Quentin visits Beatrix in custody; the case against her is collapsing under the published evidence. He returns a favor this time — arranging her defense. Final beat: inheritance redefined; what we pass on is not money but witness.
